title: Electrical, mechanical, and morphological properties of nano-filled HTV-SR/EPDM blends under AC corona aging
content:
by Muhammad Zaheer Saleem, Zulkarnain Ahmad Noorden, Lau Kwan Yiew, Ali Ahmed Salem, Abdullah S. Algamili

Among the various factors, corona discharge is recognized as one of the most threatening to degrade polymeric insulators. Over time, corona-induced deterioration has become a more dominant phenomenon in extra- and ultrahigh-voltage transmission lines. Therefore, this study investigates the aging effects on optimally balanced weight-percentage samples of high-temperature-vulcanized silicone rubber/ethylene-propylene-diene monomer (HTV-SR/EPDM) incorporating boron nitride (BN) and silicon carbide (SiC) fillers to identify the most desirable composition for resistance to degradation. The nano-sized fillers were loaded at 1, 3, and 5 wt.%. The test samples were subjected to an AC corona discharge for 72 h, utilizing a multi-needle high-voltage electrode and a plane-grounded electrode arrangement. The deterioration characteristics of the blend materials, both before and after aging, were evaluated through electrical, morphological, and mechanical analyses encompassing volume conductivity, dielectric response, scanning electron microscopy, tensile strength, and hardness measurements. The results revealed that at 8 kV stress across 30–60 °C, corona exposure increased the volume conductivity of 3 wt.% BN nanocomposites by only 25.8%–36.5%, whereas the unfilled blend experienced a much higher increase of 45.3%–88.3%. After corona exposure, high-loading nanocomposites retained up to 42.4% greater tensile strength than the degraded unfilled blend. The surface roughness was relatively lower for the filled blend samples following the corona discharge. Overall, the blend sample with 3 wt.% of BN demonstrated consistent behavior under all investigated conditions, indicating better corona-aging retardation. It has been shown that the incorporation of nano-sized fillers retards material degradation, thereby enhancing the performance of polymeric insulation.
